title: Universal Print Server Health and Printing Failures
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'Universal Print Server Health and Printing Failures' only. Does not supplant cross-domain SIEM playbooks for unrelated domains or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `linux_capacity_exceptions.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `linux_universal_print_server_health_and_printing_failu` (UC-2.6.38), SOC dashboard panel "Linux — Universal Print Server Health and Printing Failures", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:linux_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=windows` sourcetype='WinEventLog:Application' EventCode=808 where `role` satisfies detection threshold for UC-2.6.38 ('Universal Print Server Health and Printing Failures'). Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `windows` / `WinEventLog:Application` events where `role` stays below detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `linux_capacity_exceptions.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-2.6.38.

dataSources: `sourcetype="citrix:vda:events"` (`WinEventLog:Application` or CtxPrint / spooler events on VDA/UPS), `sourcetype="WinEventLog:Application"` for Citrix Print Manager Service, `sourcetype="WinEventLog:System"` for spooler service stops; `index=windows` for Universal Print forwarders if used Collected via Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows, Template for Citrix XenDesktop 7 (TA-XD7-Broker), Citrix Universal Print Server documentation-based field extractions — Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742)
spl:
index=windows OR index=xd (sourcetype="WinEventLog:Application" OR sourcetype="citrix:vda:events") (match(_raw, "(?i)Citrix.*Print|Universal Print|spooler|CtxPrint|render|driver|UPS") OR match(_raw, "(?i)printer.*(map|fail|error|offline)")) OR EventCode=808
| eval fail=if(match(_raw, "(?i)fail|error|not found|denied|offline|stuck|abort") OR match(Message, "(?i)fail|error"), 1, 0)
| eval role=if(match(_raw, "(?i)Universal Print Server|Citrix.*Print"),"UPS_VDA", "print_stack")
| where fail=1
| stats count, values(Message) as sample_msg, values(host) as hosts, earliest(_time) as first_seen, latest(_time) as last_seen by role, user, client_name, printer_name, EventCode
description: Citrix Universal Print Server offloads and compresses print traffic, but spooler instability, bad drivers, and printer auto-creation or mapping errors still break end-user print jobs. Monitoring Application and VDA event streams for spooler failures, print manager errors, and user-visible mapping failures differentiates a single bad queue from a site-wide print outage.
value: Early 'Universal Print Server Health and Printing Failures' detection reduces capacity incidents, patch regressions, and service outages by giving Linux operators a Splunk-native signal before manual triage or audit channels surface the issue.
implementation: Ingest VDA/UPS and brokering hosts into indexes with CIM-agnostic `props.conf` for long Message fields. Add printer allow/deny list lookups. Correlate with NetScaler/ADC only if you split print by site. Throttle on EventCode+printer driver hash to find systemic driver regressions. Alert when distinct hosts with fail=1 in 15m exceeds 3.
visualization: Table (failures with sample message), Pie chart (fail by driver or queue), Bar chart (failures per site).
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Patch Tuesday on `windows`** — Package managers spike `role` metrics for 'Universal Print Server Health and Printing Failures'. Correlate with apt/yum logs in the same `WinEventLog:Application` window.

2. **Nightly backup I/O on `role`** — Predictable `values` burst on fixed cron; compare `_time` minute before paging.

3. **Synthetic probe on `WinEventLog:Application`** — Nagios/Zabbix polls `role` and mimics sustained load without crossing capacity threshold.

4. **New host onboarding** — `role` baseline unstable first 48h after UF deploy.

**Suppression mechanism:** `linux_capacity_exceptions.csv` keyed on `role`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows, Template for Citrix XenDesktop 7 (TA-XD7-Broker).
• Ensure the following data sources are available: `sourcetype="WinEventLog:Application"` and `sourcetype="citrix:vda:events"` from VDAs/UPS, optional `sourcetype="WinEventLog:System"`.
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable required Windows event channels. Confirm Citrix print components log to Application. If EventCode=808 (example) is noisy, list suppressions in a macro. Tag `printer_name` and `user` with vendor extractions or `fieldalias` from XML.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust EventCode list to match your print-related Windows events):

```spl
index=windows OR index=xd (sourcetype="WinEventLog:Application" OR sourcetype="citrix:vda:events") (match(_raw, "(?i)Citrix.*Print|Universal Print|spooler|CtxPrint|render|driver|UPS") OR match(_raw, "(?i)printer.*(map|fail|error|offline)")) OR EventCode=808
| eval fail=if(match(_raw, "(?i)fail|error|not found|denied|offline|stuck|abort") OR match(Message, "(?i)fail|error"), 1, 0)
| eval role=if(match(_raw, "(?i)Universal Print Server|Citrix.*Print"),"UPS_VDA", "print_stack")
| where fail=1
| stats count, values(Message) as sample_msg, values(host) as hosts, earliest(_time) as first_seen, latest(_time) as last_seen by role, user, client_name, printer_name, EventCode
```

Step 3 — Validate
Reproduce a failed print in test and check events land in the search. Tighten regex to cut benign warnings.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Route to the print services team with driver and queue metadata. Add monthly dashboard for most failing drivers to drive packaging updates.
grandmaExplanation: We read the on-screen printer errors and system messages from your virtual session hosts — so you catch broken printers and stuck jobs before they hurt real work.
